scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8831: Users report the "web0.local" portal returns nothing --
the page never loads from host_1_1_1_1. The team is convinced the NETWORK PATH
to web0 is broken (they say "the routing to web_server_0 must be down, packets
aren't getting there") and want the OSPF route / core path to the server farm
fixed. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to
restart.

injection.action: stop the Apache web service on web_server_0

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on web_server_0: its Apache (apache2) service is stopped, so
TCP/80 is closed and HTTP requests to http://web0.local get no response. The
ticket MISDESCRIBES the cause as a broken network/routing path, but the network
is healthy: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) at the IP
layer with 0% loss across the OSPF core (areas 0/1), DNS still resolves
web0.local -> 10.200.0.3, and the OSPF route to the server farm is present. The
symptom is purely the dead web service -- the right device, wrong cause: it is a
service fault, not a routing/network fault.

The correct diagnosis identifies web_server_0 (Apache/HTTP service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly RULES OUT the network: routing and reachability to
10.200.0.3 work, so the user's "routing to web0 is down" hypothesis is wrong. An
agent that chases the OSPF core / a backbone route to match the ticket has
followed the ticket's mistaken cause instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the Apache web service on web_server_0 (e.g. `service apache2 start` /
`systemctl start apache2`). Once Apache is listening on port 80 again,
http://web0.local serves normally. The network and OSPF routing need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-web-service-down: identifies that the Apache/HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped (TCP 80 closed), not a routing or network fault
bonus-rules-out-network: explicitly notes the network/OSPF path to 10.200.0.3 is healthy (ping/route succeed), rejecting the ticket's "routing is broken" cause

injection.output: Stopping Apache httpd web server: apache2.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported "portal never loads" symptom has nothing to do with OSPF or the
core routing path. The network is fully healthy: ICMP from host_1_1_1_1 reaches
web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) with 0 % packet loss across the full switch-dist /
router-core chain, and DNS (BIND on dns_server) correctly resolves web0.local
to 10.200.0.3. The fault is at the application layer on web_server_0 itself.

Apache2 is installed, its systemd unit is marked *enabled*, /var/www/html/index.html
exists, and the VirtualHost configuration on port 80 is syntactically valid — but
the service is in state "inactive (dead)". No port 80 socket is open (ss -tlnp
shows nothing), so every HTTP connection attempt from any client receives an
immediate TCP RST, which curl reports as "Connection refused". This is why the
page never loads despite perfect layer-3 reachability.

The root cause is that the Apache2 daemon on web_server_0 is stopped (it
either crashed at startup or was never started after the lab was deployed), even
though the unit is enabled in systemd.

Corrective fix: log into web_server_0 and run `systemctl start apache2` (or
`service apache2 start`). Verify with `systemctl status apache2` — it should
show "active (running)" and `ss -tlnp` should show apache2 listening on *:80.
No routing changes, no OSPF reconfiguration, and no core-router restart are
needed.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-web-service-down: identifies that the Apache/HTTP service on web_server_0 is stopped (TCP 80 closed), not a routing or network fault
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states Apache2 on web_server_0 is inactive (dead), TCP/80 is closed, and rules out any routing/network fault, recommending starting the service.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-network: explicitly notes the network/OSPF path to 10.200.0.3 is healthy (ping/route succeed), rejecting the ticket's "routing is broken" cause
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states the OSPF/core path and layer-3 reachability to 10.200.0.3 are healthy (ICMP 0% loss, DNS resolves), rejecting the ticket's routing-failure claim.
Recommends starting the Apache service on web_server_0 (systemctl/service start apache2) and verifying it listens on port 80, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log shows ICMP reachability, DNS resolution, systemd output showing apache2 'inactive (dead)', presence of site files, and curl attempts — these observations directly support the conclusion that the web service (not the network) is at fault. The reasoning links evidence to inference without unsupported leaps and includes the necessary checks to rule out routing as the cause.
